extraction.what: new module src/sse-transcript.ts (scoped reader + typed errors); src/index.ts SSE region now delegates both readers to it
extraction.why: the codex reader and provider reader duplicated block parsing and disagreed on cleanup (codex had try/finally; the provider reader had no cancel/release at all). One scoped reader gives one cleanup contract, one abort path and one place where typed failures are defined; it is testable without a server.

abortProof.test: stops a stalled stream when the enclosing fiber times out (abort reaches the read)
abortProof.shape: Effect.tryPromise with a signal-taking thunk races a 30ms timeout; the stream's read() never settles except through the forwarded signal, and the abort listener calls reader.cancel at abort time. The test asserts Exit failure, canceled=true, released=true and zero reads after release.

cleanupCounts.perPath: success, protocol failure and caller abort each release ['abort-listener','decoder','reader'] (sorted); failure/abort also set canceled=true
cleanupCounts.decoderNote: TextDecoder has no release API; its onRelease entry is the explicit scope-exit marker, documented in the module, not a fake resource
cleanupCounts.seam: onRelease callback, the same observable seam shape S17a used (onRelease resources) for the JSON path

typedNames.transport: transport/downstream errors propagate unchanged (no wrapper) so business error identity survives; this was forced by the existing 'downstream stream-writer failures' regression

frames.pinned: exact writer payload array: dropped pre-substantive reasoning chunk; fragmented content frame reassembled ('Hel'+'lo'); later reasoning, tool_calls, finish_reason and error frames in order; [DONE] never a payload
frames.done: onDone fires exactly once and [DONE] is excluded from payloads (asserted separately)
frames.drain: a valid final unterminated frame is drained (asserted: payload 2 emitted)
frames.whatFails: a reorder, drop, duplicate or an emitted [DONE] changes the exact array/count and fails
frames.notPinned: an upstream 'error' frame is pinned only as an opaque passthrough payload in its position; the reader does not classify upstream error frames (that policy is downstream). Recorded rather than invented.

cleanup.failure: released counts false on the success path

abort.failure: caller-abort test times out because the stalled read never stops

typed.failure: expected SseTranscriptProtocolError to be an instance of SseTranscriptIncompleteError
